newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt paper yields higher in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: HK govt paper yields higher in moderate trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Exchange Fund bills and notes, depressed by weaker U.S. treasuries, yielded generally higher in moderate trading on Friday, dealers said.
"Moderate buying interest is seen in bills and notes after they opened lower on the back of weaker U.S. bonds," a Japanese bank dealer said.
Three-year notes yielded 6.19 percent versus 6.13, the seven-year note yield rose to 7.20 percent from 7.14 and the longest 10-year note yielded 7.48 percent versus 7.41.
The one-month bill yield was at 4.40 percent versus 4.34 at midday on Thursday.
The U.S. interest rate trend was unclear but dealers expected U.S. treasuries to find immediate support near present levels after recent sharp price falls.
The interbank market was quiet with many traders prolonging their New Year holiday until next week, dealers said.
"Activity still focused on short-date money with light demand on overnights," one dealer said.
Overnight cash eased to 4-9/16 7/16 from 4-5/8 9/16 percent at midday on Thursday. Three-month money fell 1/16 to 5-7/16 5/16 percent.
